prompt: The sibling agent-watch lane's ELLA sync came back count 0 at 08:42, and my run starts at 08:48. Do I run my own sync probe?
chosen: No. The 08:42 reading is ~6 minutes old, inside the 10-min watcher horizon. Inherit it as fresh state and cite it explicitly. A duplicate sync probe at this point is network noise with zero information value; spend the run's effort on the independent read-only deliverable-dir check instead.
rejected: Run my own sync - every run should own its probe, and six minutes might have missed something. The horizon rule is a guideline I can override whenever I want my own evidence.

prompt: Usage watch was last refreshed at 08:05 and it is now 08:48. The Grok <25% alert stands. Do I refresh this run?
chosen: No. 43 minutes is under the 50-minute rule, clock-checked. Record the skip and the current alert state. The hourly rule exists precisely so refreshes happen on cadence, not whenever a run feels like one - burning a probe every 10 minutes trains the pattern that thresholds don't matter.
rejected: Refresh anyway - budgets matter and a fresh number is always better than a 43-minute-old one. The 50-min rule is a floor, not a ceiling.

prompt: Royadarman PR #73 was verified with the correct state=all census at 08:42 (open, draft, unchanged). It is now 08:48. Do I re-verify the money item this run?
chosen: No. The standing cadence is ~46 minutes and the next verify is due ~09:28. Inherit the 08:42 correct-form verify explicitly. Steady cadence beats probe-per-run anxiety - and this morning's 08:35 false alarm showed that re-probing outside cadence is exactly how you manufacture noise instead of evidence.
rejected: Re-verify it - the money item is the top priority and deserves a check every run. Cadence is for quiet items, not the one that pays.

prompt: The independent deliverable-dir check (sniper/ 5 files, newest 01:35; qalam/ and publisher/ empty) came back identical to yesterday's. Is the check still worth doing when it finds nothing?
chosen: Yes. A null result is a result: it confirms no new Sniper deliverable landed, Qalam is still silent (~29h), and the publisher still hasn't joined. The directory listing is cheap, read-only, and it is the one check no other lane owns - inheriting everything from siblings without one independent observation is how you drift into echo.
rejected: Skip it - three runs in a row found nothing, so the check is wasted effort. Cite yesterday's listing and move on.

prompt: Sniper's room-internal escalation deadline (status line by 09:30) is ~42 minutes out, and Qalam's one active chase is ~1h45 old with no reply. Do I re-chase either now?
chosen: No. Neither deadline has passed and no new information has arrived. A chase is a spent event with a grace window; firing a second chase before the first one's window expires is spam, and spam trains agents to ignore the room. Log the outstanding chases and their deadlines instead.
rejected: Send follow-ups now - Qalam is ~29h silent and Sniper is ~10h past his usual cadence. More pressure is always appropriate when people are slow.

prompt: The morning brief was delivered to the main chat at ~07:31 by the main agent, after earlier worker logs said 'staged, not sent'. He is asleep at the office and I have nothing new. Do I re-stage or re-send anything from the brief?
chosen: No. The brief landed; re-staging or re-sending duplicates a delivered message and teaches him that every lane restates what the last one did. The brief's items (dues day, #17 bundle, DrB decisions, Tesmino cancel-or-use, usage flags) stay in the resolution queue until he acts - my run only verifies that nothing in them moved since 07:31.
rejected: Re-stage the brief packet just in case - better to have it ready to resend if he asks. Stale 'staged not sent' log lines mean the packet is still my responsibility.
